description:
## Context

`force_next_render` is a boolean in `Interactive` state (`interactive.ex` L129, 178) set only by the resize handler (`L489`) and consumed once in `render_frame` (`L925, 928`):

```elixir
{:ok, bytes} = Renderer.render(state.renderer, lines, cursor_seq, force: state.force_next_render)
%{state | force_next_render: false}
```

However, `Renderer.resize/3` already sets `needs_clear: true` and `previous: nil` on the renderer's own state (`renderer.ex` L185–197). The renderer's `handle_call({:render, ...})` already force-renders when `is_nil(state.previous) or state.needs_clear` (`renderer.ex` L146). So `force_next_render: true` in Interactive causes `Renderer` to force a render it would have forced anyway.

## Implementation

- Remove the `force_next_render` field from the `Interactive` `@type t` spec and `defstruct`
- Remove the `|> Map.put(:force_next_render, true)` in the resize handler
- Change the `Renderer.render/4` call in `render_frame` to `Renderer.render(state.renderer, lines, cursor_seq)` (no `force:` option)
- Remove the `%{state | force_next_render: false}` line from `render_frame`

Verify by adding a test: after `Renderer.resize/3`, the next `Renderer.render/4` call (without `force: true`) still produces a full redraw (mode `:full` in telemetry, or `full_redraws/1` increments).

## Acceptance criteria

- `force_next_render` field removed from `Interactive` struct and type
- No `force:` option passed to `Renderer.render/4` from `Interactive`
- Resize still triggers a full redraw on the next render (test-verified)
- `Renderer.render/4` public API retains the `force:` option for external callers (do not remove it from the renderer itself)
title: Eliminate force_next_render state flag — redundant with Renderer's needs_clear
